items.stem: A business sells goods on credit and issues a document requesting payment. In which book of prime entry is this transaction first recorded?

options.rationale: Correct: credit sales (evidenced by sales invoices) are first listed in the sales day book.
The cash book records receipts and payments of cash, not credit sales at the point of invoice.
The purchases day book records credit purchases, not sales.
The petty cash book records small cash payments, not credit sales.

items.explanation: Correct: credit sales (evidenced by sales invoices) are first listed in the sales day book.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: A trial balance fails to balance because a transaction was posted to the correct side but with the figures reversed between two accounts. What type of error is this best described as?

options.text: An error that a trial balance can reveal because the debits and credits no longer agree
options.rationale: Correct: if the postings no longer have equal debits and credits, the trial balance will not balance and the error is revealed.

options.text: An error of principle, which a trial balance always reveals
options.rationale: An error of principle keeps debits equal to credits, so a trial balance does not reveal it.
A compensating error is one whose effect is cancelled by another; it would still balance.
An omission leaves the trial balance in balance because nothing was posted at all.

items.explanation: Correct: if the postings no longer have equal debits and credits, the trial balance will not balance and the error is revealed.
items.domain_ref: The trial balance and correcting errors

items.stem: Select TWO items that would appear as reconciling items on a bank reconciliation statement prepared from the cash book.

options.rationale: Correct: cheques recorded in the cash book but not yet cleared by the bank are a reconciling item.
Correct: deposits recorded in the cash book but not yet on the bank statement are a reconciling item.
Credit sales do not pass through the bank and are not bank reconciliation items.
Inventory is not a cash or bank item.
Depreciation is a non-cash adjustment, not a bank reconciling item.

items.explanation: Correct: cheques recorded in the cash book but not yet cleared by the bank are a reconciling item.
